# Seth (Feng) Li — sethfengli.com

> Personal homepage of Seth (Feng) Li (李枫), a full-stack and database engineer in Sydney,
> Australia: 33 years in production across fintech, digital lending, enterprise data and AI.
> Bilingual (English / 简体中文); one URL serves both, switched client-side.

## Identity

- Full-Stack Engineer and Database Developer, DASH Technology Group (WealthTech), Sydney.
- Former CTO, AME Group — started the company's AI research group (NLP / BERT extraction of
  financial tables from unstructured PDFs) and led an ML GIS data-mining system.
- Founder of Feng Tech (fengtech.com.au), a Sydney IT services company.
- Creator of Hui Deng Zen Temple (zen.sethfengli.com), a digital Buddhist practice site.
- Master of Engineering, Computer Application Engineering (AI & Data Mining), Xiangtan University.

## Verified work

- Triumph (DASH, since 2022): re-architected the core Holdings & Performance systems in two
  passes — first 4× faster on 1/22.5 of the servers, then the same work at 1/225 of the compute
  (2,400 vCPU×6h → 16 vCPU×4h) while carrying 4× the users and volume.
- PDF Table Extractor (AME Group, 2017–2019): reconstructs tables from unstructured PDFs using
  BERT in place of CNN+LSTM for region classification, plus graph search for border detection.
- Sniper (AME Group, 2016–2018): cash-flow and valuation reporting for thousands of projects;
  .NET logic translated to VBA/Excel so analysts could model in place.
- AME Ajax (AME Group, 2018): mining & metals finance model moved from WinForms to
  .NET Core + Angular, delivered by a 6-person team in 6 months.

## Current direction (rev 2026.10, reviewed 2026-10-04)

Four positions the site argues, each with what he is building against:

1. Reliability is the whole job — a demo takes a weekend; something a regulated business will
   actually run takes a year. Retries, concurrent edits, confident wrongness and "why did the
   system decide that?" are plumbing problems, not model problems.
2. Finding the right facts beats clever reasoning — clean data, kept current, split so the
   meaning survives, under the same access rules the staff already have, with provenance.
3. Evaluation is the new regression suite — a fixed set of test questions with known good
   answers, re-run automatically on every change, failures and corrections recorded. Cost,
   speed and quality judged together.
4. Regulated verticals are the open field — most AI tooling is aimed at writing and marketing;
   banking, lending, insurance and health care are where being right matters most and a mistake
   is expensive, and where an auditable process matters more than a cleverer model.

Currently learning: agents on .NET (Microsoft agent tooling), evaluation as a release gate, and
grounded retrieval over a company's own SQL databases and documents without breaking permissions.

## Page notes for agents

- Sections in order: 01 hero, 02 about, 03 career, 04 stack, 05 projects, 06 ventures, 07 ai,
  08 insights, 09 contact. The English text is in the HTML; the Chinese is substituted at
  runtime from a dictionary, so a fetched page shows English unless the reader's browser asks
  for Chinese.
- The `ventures` section embeds two live third-party sites, each in a sandboxed frame; they load
  only on request or when scrolled into view, so a fetch of this page returns no frames.
- Performance, tenure and date claims are reconciled to a single source of truth (the Projects
  section). The page carries a revision stamp (`rev 2026.10`) and a review date
  (`2026-10-04`) that move when the content does.
- The page itself offers a keyboard search-and-jump palette (press `/`), a print view, and copy
  buttons for the contact details. Search runs locally in the browser.
- Verification tooling for this repository lives in `../tools/` (not published).
